mainTopic: An עבד as a שליח for a גט or גט שחרור, and which women are believed to bring a גט
overview: The גמרא infers that an עבד is fit to bring a גט. רבי יוחנן rules that an עבד cannot be a שליח to receive a גט for a woman, because גיטין וקידושין do not apply to him. רבי אלעזר challenges this reason from the laws of תרומה, where 'גם אתם' seems to require every שליח to be a Jew. The school of רבי ינאי answers that a שליח only needs to be a בן ברית, which an עבד is. A second report of רבי יוחנן adds a separate rule: an עבד may receive a גט שחרור for a fellow slave from a different master, but not from their shared master. The case of a pregnant שפחה whose unborn child is freed seems to contradict this rule. It is explained through רבי's view and the idea that an unborn baby is part of its mother. Then a new משנה teaches that relatives who are not believed about a husband's death are believed to bring the woman's גט, because the writing proves it. רב יוסף and אביי argue over how to reconcile this with a ברייתא, and a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא supports אביי.

steps.title: By inference, a slave is fit
steps.stepSummary: From the wording just before this line, the גמרא infers that an עבד is fit to bring a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us, by inference, that a slave is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion by drawing an inference: an עבד is fit to be a שליח to bring a גט. This sets up the next statement, which limits what an עבד can do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source being read leaves the עבד off its list of people who are unfit. That silence shows he is fit for this job. The next step adds that receiving a גט for the woman is a different matter.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; from what is implied
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew

phrases.english: By inference, a slave is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion with an inference about the עבד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד is fit to serve as a שליח to bring a גט.

steps.title: A slave cannot receive a divorce for a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, rules that an עבד cannot be a שליח to receive a גט for a woman from her husband, because he is not included in the laws of גיטין וקידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A slave cannot become an agent to receive a bill of divorce for a woman from her husband's hand, because he is not included in the laws of divorce and betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit. An עבד may bring a גט, but he cannot be the woman's שליח to receive it for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that an עבד himself is not part of the system of גיטין וקידושין. He cannot marry or divorce under Torah law. A person can act as a שליח only in a matter that applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: To receive a bill of divorce on the woman's behalf
Included in the laws of divorce and betrothal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'bringing' a גט with 'receiving' a גט. Step 1 said an עבד can bring one. Here רבי יוחנן says he cannot receive one for the woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the sugya. Is an עבד's limit based on the specific subject matter, or on his status in general?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said, Rabbi Yochanan said:
A slave cannot become an agent
to receive a bill of divorce for a woman from her husband's hand,
because he is not included in the laws of divorce and betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the fitness of an עבד from step 1 to bringing a גט only, not receiving it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד cannot be a שליח to receive a גט for a woman, since he is not included in גיטין וקידושין.

steps.title: Would a slave be fit in a matter that does apply to him?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out what רבי יוחנן's reason implies: in a matter that does apply to him, an עבד would be a fit שליח. Is that really true?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objected: The reason is that it is a matter he is not included in. So in a matter he is included in, he would be fit?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts to challenge רבי יוחנן's reason. He spells out what it implies so that he can attack it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only problem is that גיטין וקידושין do not apply to an עבד, then in a מצוה that does apply to him he should be a valid שליח. רבי אלעזר is about to show that this implication is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; he challenged it

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar objected to it:
The reason is that it is a matter he is not included in,
so in a matter he is included in, he would be fit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the implication of רבי יוחנן's reason in order to attack it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason that an עבד is unfit because he is not included in גיטין וקידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason implies that an עבד would be a fit שליח in matters that apply to him, which רבי אלעזר will show is not true.

steps.title: Proof from a gentile separating terumah
steps.stepSummary: A גוי and a כותי are included in the laws of תרומה for their own produce. Yet a גוי who separates תרומה from a Jew's produce, even with permission, has not made valid תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But consider a גוי and a כותי, who are included in the laws of תרומה for their own produce. As we learned: A גוי and a כותי who separated תרומה from their own produce, their תרומה is תרומה. And we learned: A גוי who separated תרומה from a Jew's produce, even with permission, his תרומה is not תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings two משניות as a counterexample. Being included in a מצוה is not enough to make someone a valid שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי's own תרומה counts, so the laws of תרומה do apply to him. Still, he cannot separate תרומה as a שליח for a Jew. That shows a different barrier blocks him from being a שליח. The barrier is not whether the subject applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce set aside for a כהן
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But consider a gentile and a Kuti;
who are included in the laws of terumah for their own produce,
as we learned: A gentile and a Kuti who separated terumah from their own produce,
their terumah is terumah;
and we learned: A gentile who separated terumah from a Jew's produce,
phrases.notes: He is acting as the Jew's agent here.

phrases.english: even with permission, his terumah is not terumah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the counterexample that disproves the implication raised in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Being included in a מצוה's laws does not by itself make someone a valid שליח for it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two משניות in תרומות: a גוי's own תרומה is valid, but his תרומה for a Jew is not.

steps.title: Your agents must be Jews like you
steps.stepSummary: The reason a גוי cannot be a שליח is the פסוק 'גם אתם': just as you are Jews, your agents must be Jews. So an עבד should be disqualified for that reason, even in matters that apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Is it not because it is written: 'So you also' — just as you are Jews, so too your agents must be Jews?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר finishes his challenge. He names the real source that blocks a non-Jew from being a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גם אתם' requires a שליח to be a Jew, like the person sending him. An עבד is not a full-fledged Jew, so this rule should disqualify him in every matter. That makes רבי יוחנן's narrower reason about גיטין וקידושין seem off target.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So you also' (במדבר 18:28), the source that agents must be Jews

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says an עבד cannot receive a גט because גיטין וקידושין do not apply to him. רבי אלעזר argues that the real barrier is 'גם אתם': a שליח must be a Jew. That rule would disqualify an עבד even in matters that do apply to him.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because it is written: 'So you also' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:28. Some versions have the extra word in round brackets, and some leave it out.

phrases.english: just as you are Jews,
so too your agents must be Jews?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the counterexample from step 4 and turns it back against רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since 'גם אתם' requires a שליח to be a Jew, an עבד, who is not a full Jew, should be unfit in all matters. His exclusion from גיטין וקידושין is therefore not the real reason.

steps.title: Agents must be members of the covenant, not necessarily Jews
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי reads 'גם אתם' differently: your agents must be בני ברית like you. An עבד counts as a בן ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: No. The פסוק means that just as you are members of the covenant, your agents must also be members of the covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי answers the challenge from Step 5 by reading the פסוק 'גם אתם' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 read the פסוק as 'agents must be Jews,' which would rule out an עבד completely. The school of רבי ינאי says the requirement is only being a בן ברית, a member of the covenant. A גוי is outside the covenant, but an עבד is inside it, so he can still be a שליח in matters that apply to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a גוי can never be a שליח, while an עבד can be one in matters that apply to him. It saves רבי יוחנן's reasoning.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say: No;
phrases.notes: The 'No' rejects the reading from the step before, that agents must be Jews.

phrases.english: just as you are members of the covenant,
so too your agents must be members of the covenant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 by reading the פסוק a different way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the requirement is covenant membership, not Jewishness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'גם אתם' means agents must be Jews, so an עבד could never be a שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Agents must be בני ברית. An עבד qualifies in matters that apply to him; a גוי does not.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יוחנן's ruling, with a puzzling add-on
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: an עבד cannot receive a woman's גט from her husband, 'even though' we learned that a pregnant שפחה acquires freedom for her unborn child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: An עבד cannot become a שליח to receive a woman's גט from her husband, because he is not included in the laws of גיטין and קידושין. And this is so even though we learned: if a master says 'You are a שפחה and your child is free,' and she was pregnant, she acquires freedom for the child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same ruling of רבי יוחנן from a different student, but this version has an extra line attached about a pregnant שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part repeats the ruling from Step 2. The new part is the 'even though' line about a שפחה whose unborn child is freed. It is not clear how that case connects to a woman's גט, and this sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports this version of רבי יוחנן's words
She acquired (the freedom) on his behalf

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to force the 'even though' line to fit the ruling about a woman's גט. The גמרא itself is about to ask what it is doing here.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A slave does not become an agent
to receive a woman's bill of divorce from her husband's hand,
because he is not included in the laws of divorce and betrothal,
and even though we learned:
'You are a maidservant, and your child is a free man,'
phrases.notes: The master is saying this to his own slave woman about her unborn baby.

phrases.english: if she was pregnant, she acquired freedom for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel version of רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 2, with an extra line attached.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד cannot receive a woman's גט from her husband, because he is not included in גיטין וקידושין.

steps.title: What does the pregnant maidservant line have to do with this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the line 'if she was pregnant, she acquired for him' connects to רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'if she was pregnant, she acquired for him' here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why the pregnant שפחה case is attached to a ruling about a woman's גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is about an עבד acting as a שליח between husband and wife, while the add-on is about freeing a slave's unborn child. The two topics do not obviously connect, so the גמרא asks for an explanation.

phrases.english: What is 'if she was pregnant, she acquired for him'?
phrases.notes: He means: what is this line doing next to a ruling about a woman's גט?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the puzzling add-on in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the pregnant שפחה case connects to רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן actually made two separate rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה explains that רבי יוחנן said two things. The second is that an עבד can receive a גט שחרור for a fellow slave from that slave's master, but not from his own master.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said: רבי יוחנן said two things. It seems that an עבד can receive a release document for his fellow slave from his fellow's master, but not from his own master.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the pregnant שפחה line belongs to a second, separate ruling of רבי יוחנן, about slaves receiving release documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling is the one we know, about a woman's גט. The second ruling is new: an עבד may accept freedom papers for another slave only when that slave belongs to a different master. When both belong to the same master, he may not. The pregnant שפחה line was attached to this second ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's second ruling: an עבד can receive a גט שחרור for a fellow slave from a different master, but not from their shared master.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר,
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came, he said:
Rabbi Yoḥanan said two things:

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִים דְּבָרִים שֶׁהָעֶבֶד מְקַבֵּל גֵּט לַחֲבֵירוֹ –
phrases.english: It appears that a slave may receive a bill for his fellow slave
phrases.notes: The גט here is a release document that frees a slave, not a divorce.

phrases.english: from the hand of his fellow's master,
but not from the hand of his own master.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by splitting רבי יוחנן's words into two rulings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are two rulings. The second, about receiving a גט שחרור from a shared master, is where the pregnant שפחה line belongs.

steps.title: The pregnant maidservant case seems to contradict the second ruling
steps.stepSummary: Someone might object: a teaching says a pregnant שפחה acquires freedom for her child, even though mother and child share the same master.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone whispers to you: There is a taught teaching that says if she was pregnant, she acquired freedom for the child!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יהודה's report goes on to raise a possible objection to רבי יוחנן's second ruling, using the pregnant שפחה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case the mother receives freedom for her child straight from her own master, who is also the child's master. That looks like exactly what the second ruling forbids. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Whispers to you (raises a quiet challenge)
A taught teaching (a ruling found in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: And if a person whispers to you, saying:
This is a taught teaching:
If she was pregnant, she acquired freedom for him!
phrases.notes: The mother and baby have the same master, which seems to go against the ruling just stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible contradiction to the second ruling in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that an עבד cannot receive a גט שחרור for a fellow slave from their shared master.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pregnant שפחה receives freedom for her child from their shared master, and it works.

steps.title: Two great sages already explained that case
steps.stepSummary: The reply: רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק already explained the pregnant שפחה case, so it does not disprove the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tell him: Two great sages of the generation explained this matter, רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to the objection: the pregnant שפחה case has already been explained by two great sages, so it is no real contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer only names who explained the case. Their actual explanations of why the pregnant שפחה case is different come in steps 12 and 13.

keyTerms.meaning: The great sages of the generation

steps.whatToRemember: The pregnant שפחה case does not overturn רבי יוחנן's second ruling. It has a separate explanation, which the גמרא is about to give.

phrases.english: Say to him:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר פֵּירְשׁוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר –
phrases.english: Two great ones of the generation explained the matter:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא, וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֱמוֹר לוֹ: שְׁנֵי גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר פֵּירְשׁוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 10 by pointing to an existing explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an explanation by authorities, given in the text that follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pregnant שפחה case disproves the ruling about a shared master.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two great sages explained that case, so the ruling stands.

steps.title: The pregnant maidservant teaching follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: One of the two אמוראים says the pregnant שפחה teaching follows רבי, who holds that freeing half of one's slave takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: Whose view is this? It is רבי's, who says that if someone frees half of his slave, the slave acquires freedom for that half.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of the two explanations promised in step 11. It tells us which תנא the pregnant שפחה teaching follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that freeing only part of a slave works. The baby's freedom can therefore be seen as part of the master freeing his one שפחה, not as the mother receiving a document on behalf of a separate slave. That is why the teaching does not clash with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? (Which תנא is behind this teaching?)
Someone who frees half of his slave
He acquired. Here: the freedom takes effect for that part.

phrases.english: One said: Whose view is this?
phrases.notes: "One" is one of the two sages named in step 11, רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק. "This" is the pregnant שפחה teaching.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi's, who says:
One who frees half of his slave, [the slave] acquires [freedom];

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the explanation that step 11 said already existed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the teaching to a specific תנא (רבי) whose view explains it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pregnant שפחה seems to receive freedom for her baby, a slave with the same master, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching follows רבי, for whom partial freeing works, so it is not a case of receiving for another slave.

steps.title: Why רבי holds this: the baby is part of the mother
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא explains רבי's reasoning: an unborn baby counts as part of its mother's body. So freeing her is like giving her one of her own limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: What is רבי's reason here? He holds that an unborn baby is like its mother's thigh. It is as if the master gave her one of her own limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The second sage explains the reason behind the first answer. The baby is part of the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby counts as part of the mother's body, she is not acting as a messenger for anyone else. She is receiving freedom for a part of herself. This fully removes the contradiction with רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An unborn baby is like its mother's thigh, meaning it is part of her body.

steps.whatToRemember: The pregnant שפחה is not a messenger for another slave. Her baby counts as part of her own body, so רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי בְּהָא?
phrases.english: And one said: What is Rabbi's reason in this?
He holds: a fetus is its mother's thigh,
phrases.notes: "Thigh" just means a part of her body, like any limb.

phrases.english: and it is as though he gave over to her
one of her limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the reasoning behind the answer in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning: the baby counts as part of the mother.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The baby is a separate slave, and the mother receives freedom for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The baby is part of the mother's body, so she receives freedom for herself, not as a messenger.

steps.title: The משנה: some relatives are believed to bring a woman's divorce document
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: women who are not believed to say a woman's husband died are believed to bring her גט. These are her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her צרה, her יבמה, and her husband's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the women who are not believed to say "her husband died" are believed to bring her גט: her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her יבמה, and her husband's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lists relatives who are not trusted to report a husband's death but are trusted to bring a woman's גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere these women are not believed about a husband's death, because we worry they dislike her and want to harm her. Here the משנה says that worry does not stop them from bringing her גט. The reason comes next in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her co-wife (another wife of her husband)

steps.confusionAlert: These women are not liars in general. The concern is only that they may dislike her. The משנה says that concern does not stop them from bringing a גט.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Even the women who are not believed
to say "her husband died,"
are believed to bring her bill of divorce:
her mother-in-law, and her mother-in-law's daughter,
and her co-wife, and her yevama, and her husband's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁאֵינָן נֶאֱמָנוֹת לוֹמַר מֵת בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives who are not believed about a husband's death are believed to bring the woman's גט.

steps.title: What is the difference between divorce and death?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why these women are believed about a גט but not about a death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a גט and death?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up its own explanation. It asks why the two cases are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases free the woman to remarry, so it seems the same worry should apply to both. The question points to a difference that the answer will name.

phrases.english: What is the difference between a bill of divorce and death?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why these women are believed about a גט but not about a death.

steps.title: The written document proves it
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that with a גט, the writing itself is proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the writing proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. A גט is a written document that backs up the messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a death report, everything rests on the woman's word, so a possible grudge matters. With a גט, the document itself shows the husband divorced her. The woman bringing it is not the only basis.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main reason for the whole משנה. The written document makes the messenger's trustworthiness much less important.

phrases.english: That the writing proves [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The written גט backs up the testimony. A death report has no document.

steps.title: A woman may bring her own divorce document
steps.stepSummary: Going further, the woman herself may bring her own גט, as long as she states "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם".
steps.simpleTranslation: The woman herself may bring her own גט, provided she says: "It was written in front of me and signed in front of me."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another rule. Even the woman herself can bring her own גט, with one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the document proves the divorce, even the person who benefits from it can deliver it. She must still make the standard statement that a messenger makes, as the גמרא will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: It was written in front of me and signed in front of me

steps.whatToRemember: A גט can be brought by relatives who are not trusted about a death, and even by the woman herself, because the writing is proof. She must still say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

phrases.english: The woman herself may bring her bill of divorce,
provided that she must say:
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reasoning of step 16 to the woman herself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman may bring her own גט if she states בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

steps.title: A teaching says these women are not believed to bring the divorce document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה from a ברייתא: just as these women are not believed about a death, they are not believed to bring the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: just as they are not believed to say "her husband died," so they are not believed to bring her גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that a ברייתא says the opposite of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separated the two cases, and the ברייתא treats them the same. This is a direct contradiction about the very same women.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the discussion of the משנה
But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But isn't it taught:
Just as they are not believed to say "her husband died,"
so they are not believed to bring her bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that these relatives are believed to bring a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that these same women are not believed, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Israel versus outside Israel
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is no contradiction. The משנה is talking about ארץ ישראל and the ברייתא is talking about חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. Here, in ארץ ישראל. There, outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction. Each source is talking about a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, which believes them, is about a גט brought within ארץ ישראל. The ברייתא, which does not believe them, is about a גט brought from outside the land. The גמרא will go on to explain why location makes this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
Here... there (each source applies to a different case)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult:
here, in the Land [of Israel];
phrases.notes: "Here" means our משנה, which believes these women.

phrases.english: there, outside the Land.
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא, which does not believe them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into different cases by location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are ruling on the same case and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about ארץ ישראל and the ברייתא is about חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: רב יוסף explains why the location matters
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains his distinction. In ארץ ישראל we do not rely on the woman's word, so she is believed. Outside ארץ ישראל we rely on her word, so she is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל, where we do not rely on her statement, she is believed. Outside ארץ ישראל, where we do rely on her statement, she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is filling in the reason behind רב יוסף's answer from the last step: why would ארץ ישראל and חוץ לארץ give different results?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל the woman bringing the גט does not have to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, so the גט does not stand on her word. She is just carrying it. Outside ארץ ישראל her statement is what makes the גט valid. Since a woman who hates the wife might lie, we cannot let the whole thing depend on her.

keyTerms.meaning: her own statement (here, saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם)

phrases.english: In the Land [of Israel], where it is not on her own statement
phrases.notes: In ארץ ישראל the messenger does not need to say "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם" at all.

phrases.english: that we rely, she is believed;
outside the Land, where it is on her own statement
that we rely, she is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאָרֶץ – דְּלָאו אַדִּיבּוּרַהּ דִּידַהּ קָא סָמְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב יוסף's answer in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by location, and explaining why the location matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה (believed) and the ברייתא (not believed) seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about ארץ ישראל, where her word is not relied on. The ברייתא is about חוץ לארץ, where her word decides everything.

steps.title: אביי argues the reasoning should be reversed
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the opposite makes more sense. In ארץ ישראל the husband's challenge counts, so a hostile woman could use the גט to cause harm, and she is not believed. Outside ארץ ישראל his challenge is ignored, so she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary, the opposite makes more sense! In ארץ ישראל, if the husband comes and challenges the גט, we listen to him. So we can say she means to cause trouble, and she is not believed. Outside ארץ ישראל, if the husband comes and challenges, we do not listen to him, so she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's reasoning. He keeps the split between ארץ ישראל and חוץ לארץ but flips which place is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's worry is not whether the גט stands on her word. His worry is whether she can use it to hurt the wife. In ארץ ישראל the husband can still challenge the גט later. A hostile woman could bring it, let the wife remarry, and then the husband's challenge would ruin her. Outside ארץ ישראל, once בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם is said, the husband's challenge is ignored, so there is no harm she can cause.

keyTerms.meaning: on the contrary, the opposite makes more sense

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רב יוסף agree that the answer depends on ארץ ישראל versus חוץ לארץ. They only argue about which place is the one where she is believed.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, the opposite is reasonable!
In the Land, where if the husband comes and contests,
we pay attention to him, where one can say
she intends to cause damage, she is not believed;
phrases.notes: She would get the wife to remarry on a גט the husband could later knock down.

phrases.aramaic: בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, דְּאִי אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעַר –
phrases.english: outside the Land, where if the husband comes and contests,
we do not pay attention to him, she is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reasoning from step 20 and offers the reverse distinction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects which place רב יוסף assigned to the משנה and which to the ברייתא, but keeps the idea of splitting by location.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The real danger is the hostile woman causing harm. That danger exists only where the husband can still challenge the גט, which is in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי עקיבא proves with a קל וחומר that the wife can bring her own גט. Its starting point is that the hostile women are believed to bring it, which matches אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with אביי: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי עקיבא: A woman is believed to bring her own גט, through a קל וחומר. If the women who the חכמים said are not believed to say "her husband died" are still believed to bring her גט, then she herself, who is believed to say "her husband died," should surely be believed to bring her own גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for אביי's side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is only needed where her word actually matters. That means outside ארץ ישראל, where she must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. In that very case the ברייתא takes for granted that the hostile women ARE believed to bring the גט. That fits אביי, who said they are believed outside ארץ ישראל, and not רב יוסף, who said they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
a 'how much more so' argument: from a weaker case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: hostile women are believed in ארץ ישראל but not outside it. אביי: the reverse, because the danger is the husband's later challenge. The ברייתא of רבי עקיבא supports אביי.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once the ברייתא sides with אביי, his reading becomes the stronger position in the sugya: the concern about these women is the harm they could cause, not whether the גט depends on their word.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה נֶאֱמֶנֶת לְהָבִיא גִּיטָּהּ – מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: A woman is believed to bring her own bill of divorce, through a 'how much more so' argument:
Just as the women about whom the Sages said
they are not believed to say "her husband died"
are believed to bring her bill of divorce;
she, who is believed to say "her husband died",
is it not logical that she is believed to bring her own bill of divorce?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting אביי's view from step 21.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the hostile women are believed to bring the גט outside ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי עקיבא, which builds a קל וחומר on the fact that the hostile women are believed to bring the גט
